whatThePageStates: The page is a two-section landing topic that defines the eligibility envelope for Amazon Macie sensitive data discovery of S3 objects: an object must sit in a general purpose bucket, use a supported S3 storage class, AND use a supported file or storage format, otherwise it is an 'unclassifiable object' that Macie skips. Section one is a six-bullet list of supported S3 storage classes plus a prose sentence that explicitly names S3 Glacier Deep Archive and S3 Express One Zone as unsupported ('such as', so non-exhaustive) and excludes S3 directory buckets entirely. Section two is a five-row table whose columns are File or storage type / Description / File name extensions, enumerating 22 supported file name extensions across five type groupings, with the Text row ending in 'and others' so that row is open-ended. A closing sentence explicitly states that Macie does not analyse images, audio, video or other multimedia, but names no extensions for them. Repeated prose confirms the same rules apply to both sensitive data discovery jobs and automated sensitive data discovery, and to both managed and custom data identifiers.

features.featureName: Supported Amazon S3 storage classes for sensitive data discovery
features.statuses: 6 Yes, 2 No; 6+2=8. The 6 Yes are the bullets under 'Supported Amazon S3 storage classes': Reduced Redundancy (RRS), S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, S3 Intelligent-Tiering, S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA), S3 Standard, S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). The 2 No are named in prose as explicit exclusions: S3 Glacier Deep Archive and S3 Express One Zone. No Partial values exist. Important caveat: the No side is introduced with 'such as', so it is illustrative, not the complete unsupported set — every other real S3 storage class (e.g. S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval) is simply ABSENT from the page and must not be scored as a stated No. If a measurement wants stated-supported only, the number is 6.
features.scope: Bucket type is a real second dimension: the whole claim is scoped to S3 general purpose buckets, and S3 directory buckets are excluded outright regardless of class. A second scope is the discovery method — the page says the identical rules hold for sensitive data discovery jobs and for automated sensitive data discovery, and for both managed and custom data identifiers, so the scope does not vary the answer per storage class.
features.reasoning: The enumerated thing is the Amazon S3 storage class, a universe S3 owns and publishes independently of Macie, so the axis is the external 'storageClass'. The unit of claim is one storage class per bullet — each bullet names exactly one class, there is no many-to-one grouping, and the claim per class is binary can-Macie-analyse-objects-in-it.

features.featureName: Supported file and storage formats for sensitive data discovery
features.statuses: 22 Yes, 0 stated No, 0 Partial; 22+0+0=22. Counted from the 'File name extensions' column, row by row: Big data 2 (.avro, .parquet) + Compression or archive 4 (.gz, .gzip, .tar, .zip) + Document 5 (.doc, .docx, .pdf, .xls, .xlsx) + Email message 1 (.eml) + Text 10 (.csv, .htm, .html, .json, .jsonl, .tsv, .txt, .xml, .yaml, .yml) = 2+4+5+1+10 = 22. No extension is duplicated across rows. The Text row ends with 'and others', so 22 is a stated floor, not a closed set. The only stated not-supported content is the sentence 'Macie doesn't analyze data in images, or audio, video, and other types of multimedia content' — that is a category exclusion naming ZERO extensions, so it contributes no countable No values and must not be inflated into a list of .jpg/.mp4/etc.
features.scope: Same two scopes as the storage-class feature and both are non-differentiating: it applies to jobs and to automated sensitive data discovery alike, and to managed and custom data identifiers alike. A related but separate mechanic, not a coverage scope, is nested inspection of compression/archive files (up to 1,000,000 files, 10 nesting levels) — that is a quota, not a per-format status.
features.reasoning: Two granularities are available on this page: five file/storage TYPE rows and 22 file name extensions. The extension is the finer, externally-owned, actually-testable unit — an operator asks 'will Macie read my .parquet file', not 'does Macie support the Big data category' — and AWS itself provides the extension column as the enumeration. So the axis is the external 'fileExtension' with 22 values. Note this is the inverse of the row-collapse trap: rows are COARSER than the axis (5 rows expand to 22 extensions), not finer, so distinctTargets/collapse do not apply and are omitted. If a measurement instead chose the type grouping as its unit, the number would be 5 — but that count is a table artefact, not a coverage universe.

shouldNotExtract: The 'Topics' bullet list at the top (2 nav links to the page's own anchors) is navigation, not coverage. The Tip box about exporting RDS/Aurora snapshots or DynamoDB tables to S3 is a workaround suggestion and asserts no support for RDS, Aurora or DynamoDB — harvesting those as three supported services would be flatly wrong. The Description column of the format table is prose gloss, not an axis. The quota numbers (1,000,000 files, nested depth of 10) are limits, not coverage values. The repeated 'unclassifiable object' definition paragraphs appear twice, once per section, and are the same statement duplicated — do not double count. The link to filtering the S3 bucket inventory, the link to the S3 storage classes user guide, the RFC 2822 link, and the entire 'See also' block about Agent Toolkit skills and the aws agent-toolkit search-skills CLI command are boilerplate with zero coverage content.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page never mentions a Region, an AWS Region table, a partition, or any geographic availability — any per-Region figure attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: effectively nothing enumerable. Only Amazon S3 is the analysed service and it is the fixed context, not a member of an enumerated list; the Tip's mentions of RDS, Aurora and DynamoDB are export workarounds, explicitly NOT Macie coverage of those services. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing enumerable either. The page fixes a single implicit resource type — the S3 object in a general purpose bucket — and its only resource-shaped statement is the exclusion of S3 directory buckets; that is one boundary sentence, not a resource-type matrix. What the page does give, and gives well, are two independent format/class universes: 6 stated-supported (+2 stated-unsupported) S3 storage classes, and 22 stated-supported file name extensions grouped into 5 type rows.
trap: The single most likely misparse is counting the format table's 5 rows as 5 supported formats and reporting '5' as the coverage number, when the table's own extensions column names 22 distinct extensions — the rows are groupings coarser than the axis, the reverse of the usual row-collapse trap. Runners-up: (1) treating the storage-class 'such as S3 Glacier Deep Archive or S3 Express One Zone' sentence as a complete unsupported list, and so scoring every unnamed S3 class as a stated No when it is merely absent; (2) turning 'Macie doesn't analyze data in images, or audio, video, and other types of multimedia content' into invented extension rows (.jpg, .mp4, .mp3) that the page never writes; (3) merging the two sections into one number such as 6+22=28, when they are two independent axes that are ANDed at evaluation time, not summed; (4) harvesting the Tip as Macie support for Amazon RDS, Aurora and DynamoDB; (5) counting the duplicated 'unclassifiable object' paragraph twice, or reading the two 'Topics' nav bullets as two coverage items; (6) mistaking the 1,000,000-file / 10-level nesting quota for a coverage count.
